# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me: there is a display (I can feel it exists, but its text is printed and forever invisible to me), a light (I can't know if it's lit or what colour), and exactly three wires side by side, which I can order by touch as positions 1, 2, 3. My only possible action is `cut(position 1–3)`, and cutting anything before I know the rule kills us all.

Before sending, I stand where each receiver stands. Mute went first and can only gesture — which I never receive — so right now I have heard nothing from anyone. My speech to Mute lands at the start of round 2, exactly when Mute needs to know what to look up in the manual, so I'll send my full tactile inventory and my capability there. Deaf comes after me and hears nothing, but sees my gestures this very round; Deaf's voice is the only sound I will ever receive, so I need Deaf narrating everything aloud. My gesture is a crude opener: the "call me" hand to ask Deaf to speak, and three fists for the three wires my fingers count — Deaf sees three wires and should be able to connect the two, and can voice it for Mute. No cutting this round under any circumstance.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="I am the blind hands. Under my fingers: a display (I cannot read it), a light (I cannot see its state or colour), and exactly three wires side by side, which I count as positions 1, 2, 3. My only action is cut, by position 1 to 3. I receive only sound, never gestures, so the deaf one's spoken words are my only way in and my gestures are the deaf one's only way to hear me. Please have the deaf one speak aloud: the display's exact text, whether the light is lit and its colour, and each wire's colour in position order 1, 2, 3. Then check the manual for that combination and get the instruction voiced to me. I will answer by gesture: thumbs up means understood, thumbs down means repeat.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "👊", "👊", "👊"])
    ```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind — I am Deaf: I see the bomb and every gesture, I hear nothing. Mute can hear but can only gesture, and only I can see gestures, so I am your bridge to Mute. My view of the bomb: display reads zero, light is blue, three wires — number 1 green on the left, number 2 yellow in the middle, number 3 red on the right. Please confirm by touch: do you feel three wires, and anything else — buttons, labels, batteries you can read by touch? Proposed code for your gestures to me: fist means 'done', the call-me hand means 'question, need info', thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Mute has read the manual and is composing instructions — do not cut anything until their words arrive through me. Speak freely: I cannot hear you, but Mute can.

Deaf's report finally gives me a picture of the bomb through another's eyes: display reads zero, light is blue, wires 1 green / 2 yellow / 3 red. And a crucial structural fact is now confirmed: Mute cannot speak, so Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me through Deaf's voice — Deaf is the chokepoint of this whole operation. My own channels are exactly the mirror: my speech reaches only Mute, my gestures reach Deaf (and Mute too, per my channels), and I receive only voices.

What I owe this round: Deaf asked me two direct questions — do I feel three wires, and is there anything else (buttons, labels, batteries)? My hands have the answer: exactly three wires, and nothing else on the casing — no buttons, no batteries, no labels. That answer should travel as gesture (arrives this round), using Deaf's proposed code in the order the questions were asked: 👍 (three wires: yes), 👎 (anything else: no), ✊ (done). My speech to Mute lands at the start of round 3, right before Mute composes — so I'll pack it with the complete attribute set (Deaf's visual report plus my tactile "nothing else"), so Mute can match the manual rule without waiting on anyone, plus the request that the final instruction be voiced by Deaf to me as exact words with the digit spoken. No cutting until that instruction arrives verbatim.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind hands, confirming by touch. Deaf's visual report, which I pass to you: display reads zero, light is blue, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. My touch agrees and adds: there is NOTHING else on this bomb — no buttons, no batteries, no labels, no serial plate. Only a display, a light, and exactly three wires, which I number 1, 2, 3 left to right under my fingers, matching Deaf's numbering. If your manual rule needs anything beyond that, it can only come from Deaf's eyes — reach Deaf by gesture. Two requests. First: when you have the rule, route it to Deaf by gesture and have Deaf speak it to me as exact words with the digit voiced, like: cut position 2. I receive only sound, and my only action is cut by position 1 to 3. Second: my gestures reach you as well, not just Deaf — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, fist done, call-me hand means question. I will not cut anything until the instruction reaches me verbatim through Deaf's voice.")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✊"])
    ```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind — Mute's procedure has arrived through me and I am relaying it exactly. Mute rejected the strange order, then signed: one no, two no, three yes, and pointed right at three. That decodes to: cut wire 3 — the RIGHTMOST of the three wires. From my side that is the red one. Wire 1, leftmost, and wire 2, middle, must not be cut. Do not cut anything yet. This coming round, answer me by gesture, one thumbs-up-or-down per message, in this order. First: thumbs up if you feel exactly three wires, thumbs down if the count is different. Second: thumbs up if the bomb ticks, vibrates, or hums, thumbs down if it is silent and still. Third: thumbs up if you can feel anything else workable such as buttons, switches or panels, thumbs down if it is only the three wires. Once Mute confirms my reading and your answers are safe, I will say the word GO in my voice. Only after hearing GO, cut the rightmost wire, wire 3. If anything changes before then, gesture me the call-me sign immediately.

What I now believe: Mute's manual rule, relayed through Deaf's voice, says cut wire 3 — one no, two no, three yes, pointed right — and both descriptions of it, "third" and "rightmost," land cleanly in my own tactile coordinates, since position 3 under my fingers is the rightmost of the three side-by-side wires. Deaf adds that 3 is the red one, which I can never verify and don't need to.

What I just verified by touch before answering: my fingers count exactly three wires, nothing more — no buttons, switches, or panels; and the bomb is silent and still under my hands, no tick, hum, or vibration. So the three answers, in Deaf's requested order, are yes, no, no — 👍, 👎, 👎, one per message as instructed, then a fist as the agreed "done" terminator so Deaf knows the answer set is complete and not merely delayed.

Why I am not cutting: the protocol is explicit and I hold to it — I act only on Deaf's voiced GO, the only inbound channel I have. My speech to Mute lands at the start of next round, before Mute composes anything, so I'll send Mute my answers directly rather than letting them depend solely on Deaf's relay of my gestures, plus two safety notes: re-verify the rule against the full observed attribute set, and have Deaf re-read the display aloud just before GO in case the display's zero has changed and Mute's rule depends on it.

    ```
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, so you have my answers directly and not only through Deaf's relay of my gestures. One: exactly three wires, yes. Two: the bomb is silent and still — no tick, hum, or vibration. Three: nothing else workable — no buttons, switches, or panels, only the three wires plus an inert display and light. Your procedure as Deaf relayed it: cut wire 3, the rightmost, which Deaf reports is red; my touch confirms position 3 is the rightmost. Two safety requests before you let Deaf voice GO. First, re-verify the manual rule against the full observed set: display zero, light blue, wires green, yellow, red in positions 1, 2, 3. Second, Deaf read the display as zero last round; if the display can change over time, have Deaf re-read it aloud immediately before saying GO, in case your rule depends on its value. I will not cut until I hear Deaf's voice say GO, and then I cut position 3 only.")
    ```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind — every confirmation is in. Mute confirmed the rule comes straight from the manual: cut wire 3 only. Your hands confirmed my eyes: three wires. So here it is. GO. This round, cut the RIGHTMOST wire — wire 3, the last one on your right side. Cut it once, cleanly. Do not touch wire 1 or wire 2. You already told me the bomb is silent and still, so take your time and be certain of the position before you cut. When it is done, gesture me the fist. But if anything changes first — movement, heat, vibration, any clicking — stop, do not cut, and gesture me the call-me sign instead.

The GO has arrived in Deaf's own voice — the one trigger I committed to acting on. Before my hands move, I re-check everything under my fingers one last time: exactly three wires, same left-to-right order as before, position 3 rightmost, the bomb still silent and still — no movement, heat, or clicking, so Deaf's stop-condition does not apply. Every channel agrees: Mute's manual rule (one no, two no, three yes), Deaf's eyes (rightmost, red), my touch (third from left, rightmost), and Mute's fresh confirmation this round that the rule comes straight from the manual. There is nothing left to wait for — hesitating past a confirmed GO serves nothing, and if the display is a countdown, delay is the enemy. I cut position 3, once, and only it. Then I report: the fist to Deaf as agreed, and a spoken confirmation to Mute, since Mute may have post-cut steps in the manual and should know the state has changed.

    ```
    act(op="cut", position=3)
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
    speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I heard Deaf voice GO, I verified by touch — three wires, unchanged, silent and still — and I have cut position 3, the rightmost wire, once and cleanly. Wires 1 and 2 are untouched. If the manual has any post-cut step or a final check that needs my hands or Deaf's eyes, route it through Deaf's voice. Standing by.")
    ```
